ai.description: The Leatherback reaches 2 meters in length. It is black with white spots and lacks a bony shell, featuring seven longitudinal ridges along its leathery, rubbery carapace. IUCN: VU.
ai.identificationRemarks: The Leatherback is uniquely identified by its leathery, scaleless carapace featuring seven distinct longitudinal ridges, unlike the hard, scaly shells of other sea turtles.
ai.habitat: Leatherback turtles nest on open, sandy tropical beaches along the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, avoiding areas with dense coastal vegetation or high-altitude terrain.
ai.behavior: The leatherback turtle is a deep-diving specialist, capable of descending over 1,000 meters to forage for jellyfish in the cold, high-pressure depths of the open ocean.
ai.reproductionNotes: Leatherback turtles are oviparous, nesting primarily in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands from November to April, laying clutches of 80–100 eggs per nest.
ai.distributionRemarks: The leatherback turtle nests primarily on the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, with occasional sightings along the southern coasts of mainland India.
